findings.title: tr() miniscript leaves are accepted and given an address but tr-leaf-satisfaction has no miniscript case, so they are unspendable
findings.core_does: SignTaprootScript satisfies EVERY tapscript leaf through miniscript::FromScript(script, ms_satisfier) followed by ms->Satisfy(...) (sign.cpp:529-541). pk/pkh/multi_a are not special-cased at all in Core's signer; they are just miniscript fragments, so an arbitrary miniscript leaf signs by the same code path as a pk() leaf.
findings.we_do: %parse-descriptor-body routes a tr() leaf into %parse-miniscript-descriptor with :tapscript (descriptors.lisp:884-886), so tr(K,{...,<miniscript>}) parses, passes the IsSane gate, and derives an address. But tr-leaf-satisfaction (descriptors.lisp:1396) is a hand-written CASE over out-desc-kind covering only :pk, :pkh, :multi-a and :sortedmulti-a. A leaf of kind :miniscript falls through the CASE and returns NIL, i.e. 'unsatisfiable'. Its own docstring still says 'We have no tapscript miniscript', which stopped being true when the tapscript miniscript context was added.
findings.impact: The wallet hands out a receive address for a tr() descriptor whose script-path leaf it can never spend, even holding every private key. Coins in that leaf are recoverable only by moving the descriptor and keys to Core (or to another implementation). Every other leaf kind in the same tree still spends, so the failure is silent: the signer reports the input unsigned rather than erroring.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval, warm image. (1) parse-descriptor of tr(0279be66...,{pk(03d30199...),and_v(v:pk(03fff97b...),older(10))}) returned (:OK :KIND :TR :SCRIPTS ("5120a3290bab930ad7be5758c45a98261201d0912b1ffb81470c9a7c941fd1bab2f7")) -- accepted, address derived. (2) out-desc-tree leaf kinds were (:PK :MINISCRIPT). (3) tr-leaf-satisfaction on each leaf with a signer that returns a 64-byte signature for ANY key returned ((:PK (#(7 ... 64 bytes))) (:MINISCRIPT NIL)) -- the miniscript leaf produces no witness.

findings.title: A miniscript descriptor's node reports script size 0, so IsValid's MaxScriptSize gate never fires for any descriptor
findings.core_does: internal::Parse accumulates script_size from the FRAGMENT SHAPE, independently of whether a key is a literal or a key expression: +34 per P2WSH key in multi(), +34/+33 for pk(), +24 for pkh(), +5 for andor(, and so on (miniscript.h:1865-2090). It compares it against internal::MaxScriptSize(ctx) (=MAX_STANDARD_P2WSH_SCRIPT_SIZE 3600 outside tapscript, miniscript.h:282-294) at the top of every parse step (miniscript.h:1912) and inside the wrapper loop (:1931), and returns {} the moment it is exceeded. Node::IsValid() then re-checks ScriptSize() <= MaxScriptSize (:1670-1673).
findings.we_do: make-ms-node computes script-size as (length (ms-node-script node)) and gives up -- setting it to 0 -- whenever any key in the subtree is not a byte sequence (miniscript.lisp:586-593). Inside a descriptor, *ms-key-parser* is bound so every key is a desc-key STRUCT, so every node of every miniscript descriptor reports script-size 0. ms-node-valid-p then evaluates 0 <= 3600, which is always true, so the size half of Core's IsValid is dead for exactly the inputs that reach the RPC. Ops and stack limits still work (they are computed from the tree shape), so the descriptor also passes IsSane.
findings.impact: importdescriptors / getdescriptorinfo / deriveaddresses accept a wsh(<miniscript>) descriptor whose witnessScript exceeds MAX_STANDARD_P2WSH_SCRIPT_SIZE, which Core refuses outright. The wallet then derives addresses from it and receives to them; any spend is non-standard (IsWitnessStandard rejects a witnessScript over 3600 bytes), so the coins will not relay and are effectively stuck. The same hole disables the 329482-byte tapscript ceiling for tr() leaves.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval, warm image. Built wsh(and_v(v:multi(1,K1..K20),and_v(v:multi(1,K21..K40),...))) with six multi() fragments over 120 distinct derived pubkeys (8143-character descriptor). parse-descriptor returned (:ACCEPTED T :NODE-SCRIPT-SIZE 0 :VALID-P T :SANE-P T :EXPANDED-SPK-LEN 34) and ms-node-script of the same node with a concrete key function produced a 4104-byte witnessScript -- 504 bytes over the 3600 limit Core enforces during Parse.

findings.title: ms-parse never checks fragment arity: extra arguments are silently dropped and missing ones raise an unhandled TYPE-ERROR
findings.core_does: Parse pushes an exact schedule of ParseContext entries per fragment -- CLOSE_BRACKET, WRAPPED_EXPR, COMMA, WRAPPED_EXPR for the binary combinators (miniscript.h:2060-2090) and one more WRAPPED_EXPR/COMMA pair for andor (:2043-2051). COMMA fails unless the next character is ',' and CLOSE_BRACKET fails unless it is ')' (:2189-2199), so and_v(X,Y,Z) is a parse failure at the third comma and and_v(X) is a parse failure at the missing one. ComputeType additionally CHECK_NONFATALs n_subs per fragment (miniscript.cpp:60-71).
findings.we_do: ms-parse splits the argument list on top-level commas and hands the whole list to make-ms-node (miniscript.lisp:1180-1190) without ever checking its length. ms-compute-type reads only x, y and z, ms-node-script only (sub 0) and (sub 1), so a THIRD argument to and_v/and_b/or_b/or_c/or_d/or_i (or a fourth to andor, or a second key to pk()/pk_k()/pkh(), or a second number to older()/after()) is dropped and the node types and compiles as though it were not written. In the other direction a MISSING argument leaves (nth 1 subs) NIL, which every downstream walker dereferences: ms-node-ops does (+ count NIL) and ms-node-to-string calls an ms-node accessor on NIL.
findings.impact: A descriptor string that Core refuses is accepted here as a DIFFERENT, strictly weaker policy: wsh(and_v(v:pk(A),older(10),pk(B))) is stored and addressed as and_v(v:pk(A),older(10)), so the branch the operator wrote to require B is gone and A alone can spend after 10 blocks. Nothing in the accept path warns; only re-reading the normalized string in getdescriptorinfo would reveal it. In the too-few-arguments direction the descriptor RPCs answer -32603 'Internal error' from a raw Lisp TYPE-ERROR instead of Core's parse error.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval, warm image. ms-parse "and_v(v:pk(03d30199..),older(10),pk(03fff97b..))" -> (:PARSED :VALID T :TOPLEVEL T :STR "and_v(v:pk(03d30199..),older(10))" :SCRIPTLEN 37); "andor(0,1,1,pk(K))" -> "andor(0,1,1)"; "or_i(0,1,pk(K))" -> "l:1"; "pk(K1,K2)" -> "pk(K1)"; "older(10,99)" -> "older(10)". parse-descriptor of wsh(and_v(v:pk(K))), wsh(or_b(pk(K))), wsh(andor(1,1)) and wsh(thresh(1,pk(K),and_v(v:pk(K)))) each returned (:ERROR TYPE-ERROR "The value NIL is not of type BITCOIN-LISP.VALIDATION::MS-NODE"); src/rpc/server.lisp:1152 turns that into HTTP 500 / -32603.

findings.title: Miniscript parsing and inference are cubic in input size and have no incremental script-size ceiling
findings.core_does: Two independent bounds. (a) Node::CalcScriptLen / ComputeScriptLen derives a node's script length in O(1) from its fragment, its first sub's type and the SUM of its subs' lengths (miniscript.cpp:265-297), cached once in the constructor. (b) Parse carries a running script_size that borrows one byte from every leaf so that every fragment increases it, and returns {} as soon as script_size > MaxScriptSize(ctx) -- checked at the top of the parse loop (miniscript.h:1912) and again per wrapper character (:1931). FromScript likewise refuses a script larger than MaxScriptSize before decomposing it (:2692).
findings.we_do: make-ms-node computes script-size as (length (ms-node-script node)) (miniscript.lisp:589), and ms-node-script re-serializes the WHOLE subtree from scratch every time. Since make-ms-node runs once per node, total work is sum over i of O(i^2) = O(n^3) in the size of the expression. ms-parse has no running size bound at all and no length limit on its input, and ms-from-script does not refuse an oversized script before decomposing it; the only ceiling is the per-step ms-node-valid-p bail inside the decode loop, which still costs the cubic work up to that point.
findings.impact: Any authenticated RPC that parses a descriptor (getdescriptorinfo, deriveaddresses, importdescriptors, scantxoutset) or infers a miniscript from a supplied witnessScript (signrawtransactionwithkey / walletprocesspsbt via rawtransaction.lisp:469, and wallet coin sizing via wallet-spend.lisp:489) can be made to burn minutes to hours of CPU in one RPC worker from a single request. The RPC body cap is 32 MiB (src/rpc/server.lisp:692), so the input is not meaningfully bounded; a handful of concurrent requests exhausts the RPC worker pool. Core answers the same inputs in microseconds because it stops at 3600 accumulated script bytes.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval, warm image, wall clock inside the image. ms-parse of "n:" repeated N times followed by "1": N=500 (1001 chars) 120 ms; N=2000 (4001 chars) 6273 ms; N=5000 (10001 chars) 98000 ms -- and the N=5000 case is INVALID (script 5001 bytes > 3600), i.e. 98 seconds spent to reach a verdict Core reaches after 3600 bytes. ms-from-script of OP_1 followed by N OP_0NOTEQUAL: 501 bytes 122 ms; 2001 bytes 6443 ms; 3601 bytes 36929 ms (returning NIL). Scaling is ~n^3 in both directions.

findings.title: An inferred pk_h node carries no key, so a P2WSH miniscript with a pkh() branch can never be signed
findings.core_does: DecodeScript resolves the 20-byte hash back to a real key through the context: auto key = ctx.FromPKHBytes(in[2]...); if (!key) return {}; and stores it in the PK_H node (miniscript.h:2331-2339). For the signer that context is WshSatisfier::FromPKHBytes -> Satisfier::CPubFromPKHBytes, which looks the CKeyID up in the SigningProvider and records a missing_pubkeys entry when it is absent (sign.cpp:428-436, 479-482). ProduceInput's PK_H arm then has both the key bytes and a signable key (miniscript.h:1252-1256).
findings.we_do: ms-from-script emits (make-ms-node :pk-h :data keyhash) with an EMPTY keys list (miniscript.lisp:1817). ms-produce-input's :pk-h arm then evaluates (first (ms-node-keys node)) = NIL and calls the satisfier's sign-fn with NIL, and builds the key element as (ms-stack-of (funcall key-fn NIL)) = a stack element whose value is NIL. The docstring at miniscript.lisp:1811 says 'a satisfier looks the key up by it [the hash]'; no satisfier does -- there is no hash-to-key lookup anywhere in the satisfier or in its two callers.
findings.impact: compute-input-signatures' miniscript arm (src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:469-485) looks the key up as (gethash NIL pubmap), always misses, and reports the pk_h branch unavailable, so a P2WSH miniscript containing pkh()/pk_h() is never signed by signrawtransactionwithkey, walletprocesspsbt or the wallet spend path even when the node holds the key -- while a policy Core signs normally. Worse, if any signer ever returns a signature for the NIL key the produced witness contains a NIL element instead of bytes, which serialization is not prepared for.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval, warm image. Parsed pkh(03d30199..), compiled to 76a914fcd35ddacad9f2d5be5e464639441c6065e6955d88ac, fed that script back to ms-from-script and satisfied it with a signer that signs any key: direct parse gave (:STACK (64 33)), the inferred node gave (:STACK (64 :NIL-ELEMENT)) -- the pubkey element is the Lisp NIL. Same for and_v(v:pk(K1),pkh(K2)): direct (64 33 64), inferred (64 :NIL-ELEMENT 64). With the real caller's pubmap lookup the signature is unavailable and the whole satisfaction fails.

findings.title: ms-from-script has no tapscript arms: no x-only key push and no multi_a decoding
findings.core_does: DecodeScript accepts a 32-byte push as a key as well as a 33-byte one (miniscript.h:2327), and has a dedicated MULTI_A arm that walks the <x> CHECKSIG (<x> CHECKSIGADD)* <k> OP_NUMEQUAL chain backwards, bounded by MAX_PUBKEYS_PER_MULTI_A (:2394-2420). FromScript is context-parameterised, so the same function serves P2WSH and tapscript.
findings.we_do: The key arm tests (eql 33 (%ms-op-push-size ops in)) only (miniscript.lisp:1800), and there is no OP_NUMEQUAL / OP_CHECKSIGADD arm anywhere in ms-from-script. A tapscript script therefore falls through to (t (fail)) at the first key push. ms-from-script also takes no context argument at all: it inherits whatever *ms-context* is bound to, and every caller leaves it at the :p2wsh default.
findings.impact: Latent today, because no caller feeds ms-from-script a tapscript leaf (the tapscript signer is the hand-rolled tr-leaf-satisfaction of finding 1141db2b, and the two P2WSH callers pass witnessScripts). It becomes load-bearing the moment tapscript leaf inference is wired -- Core's own signer is built entirely on it -- and it is the reason a straight port of Core's SignTaprootScript would silently sign nothing. It also means we cannot infer a descriptor for a taproot leaf script the way Core's InferScript does (descriptor.cpp:2806-2816).
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval, warm image, over Core's own fixed_tests corpus: 91 Test() vectors from refs/bitcoin/src/test/miniscript_tests.cpp:501-700 run in both contexts (182 runs) checking IsValid, IsValidTopLevel, exact script hex, cached-vs-computed script size, IsNonMalleable, NeedsSignature, the k property, GetOps, GetStackSize, GetWitnessSize, GetExecStackSize and the FromScript round trip. Result: (:VECTORS 91 :FAILURES 15 :BY-KIND ((:CANNOT-INFER . 15))) -- every failure is a TAPSCRIPT FromScript returning NIL, and every vector containing a key or a multi_a fails. All 167 other checks match Core exactly.

findings.title: ms-produce-input has no multi_a case, so satisfying any multi_a node is an ECASE type error
findings.core_does: ProduceInput has a MULTI_A arm (miniscript.h:1259-1284) with its own dynamic program: it signs the keys in REVERSE order (node.keys[n-1-i], because CHECKSIGADD reads the first key's signature from the top of the stack, the opposite of CHECKMULTISIG), starts sats[0] at EMPTY rather than at ZERO (there is no CHECKMULTISIG off-by-one element), and adds a ZERO per unused key.
findings.we_do: The ECASE in ms-produce-input (miniscript.lisp:1500) lists twenty-six fragments and omits :multi-a. Every other half of the miniscript implementation handles multi_a -- the type calculus, script generation, CalcOps, CalcStackSize, CalcWitnessSize and the parser all do -- so a multi_a node parses, types and compiles, and only fails when someone asks it for a witness.
findings.impact: Latent today for the same reason as 8c3b8174: ms-satisfy is only reached with P2WSH nodes, where multi_a cannot occur. But it is a hard SB-KERNEL:CASE-FAILURE, not a graceful 'no satisfaction', so as soon as ms-satisfy is wired to tr() leaves (the fix for 1141db2b) any multi_a leaf answers -32603 instead of signing. The reverse key order and the missing leading ZERO are the two details a fix has to get right.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval, warm image: ms-satisfy on (ms-parse "multi_a(1,03d30199..,03fff97b..)" :ctx :tapscript) returned (:ERROR SB-KERNEL:CASE-FAILURE ":MULTI-A fell through ECASE expression. Wanted one of (:JUST-0 :JUST-1 :PK-K :PK-H :OLDER :AFTER :SHA256 :RIPEMD160 :HASH256 :HASH160 :WRAP-A :WRAP-S :WRAP-C :WRAP-N :WRAP-D :WRAP-V :WRAP-J :AND-V :AND-B :OR-B :OR-C :OR-D :OR-I :ANDOR :MULTI :THRESH).")

findings.title: Script decomposition accepts non-minimal pushes and non-minimal script numbers that Core rejects
findings.core_does: DecomposeScript runs CheckMinimalPush(push_data, opcode) on every pushdata opcode and returns {} if it fails (miniscript.cpp:390-391), so a one-byte push of 1..16 written as 0x01 0x0a instead of OP_10 kills the whole decode. ParseScriptNumber additionally builds CScriptNum(in.second, /*fRequireMinimal=*/true) inside a try/catch (miniscript.cpp:412-421), so a number with a redundant trailing 0x00 is not a number and the fragment is not recognised.
findings.we_do: ms-decompose-script checks minimality only for OP_PUSHDATA1/2 (the (< len 76) and (< len 256) tests, miniscript.lisp:1690, 1701); the direct-push branch at miniscript.lisp:1678 accepts any 1..75-byte push without comparing it to the shortest encoding. %ms-op-number (miniscript.lisp:1729) reads up to four bytes little-endian and only rejects a set sign bit -- it never enforces CScriptNum's minimal encoding.
findings.impact: Two scripts map to one miniscript, which is exactly the property inference exists to guarantee. ms-from-script returns a node whose ms-node-script differs from the bytes it was given, so the round-trip assertion Core makes in its own test harness (miniscript_tests.cpp:468) does not hold here. The reachable consequence is bounded -- such a witnessScript is non-standard anyway under SCRIPT_VERIFY_MINIMALDATA and the recovered policy is semantically the same -- but any caller that re-derives a script or an address from an inferred node gets different bytes than it started with.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval, warm image. ms-from-script "010ab2" (non-minimal one-byte push of 10, then OP_CSV) -> (:INFERRED "older(10)" :RESER "5ab2"); ms-from-script "020a00b2" (push of [0a 00], a non-minimal CScriptNum) -> (:INFERRED "older(10)" :RESER "5ab2"). Both re-serialize to bytes different from the input. Core's own negative vectors DO pass here: the nonminpush script (miniscript_tests.cpp:650) and the non-minimal VERIFY script (:654) both return NIL, and "4c0120b1" (PUSHDATA1 of one byte) returns NIL.

findings.title: Numeric arguments accept a leading plus sign and surrounding whitespace that Core rejects
findings.core_does: Parse reads every number with ToIntegral<int64_t> over the exact argument span (miniscript.h:1878, 2018, 2027, 2039), which is locale-independent and accepts no sign, no whitespace and no partial parse. miniscript_tests.cpp:707-711 asserts this explicitly: after(-1), after(+1), thresh(-1,...) and multi(+1,...) must all fail to parse.
findings.we_do: %ms-parse-number (miniscript.lisp:1075) uses CL PARSE-INTEGER, which by default skips surrounding whitespace and accepts a leading + or -. The negative case is caught afterwards by the 0..2^32-1 range test, but a leading plus and surrounding spaces pass through.
findings.impact: Strings Core refuses are accepted, and they produce the canonical node, so the divergence is one-directional: a descriptor written against this node can fail to load in Core. The descriptor checksum covers the string as typed, so the non-canonical spelling is what gets stored and backed up.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval, warm image: ms-parse "after(+1)" -> (:PARSED :VALID T :TOPLEVEL T :STR "after(1)"); "after( 1 )" -> "after(1)"; "multi(+1,03d30199..)" -> "multi(1,03d30199..)"; "thresh(1 ,pk(03d30199..))" -> "thresh(1,pk(..))". Core asserts all four spellings are parse failures. "after(-1)" is correctly refused here.

findings.title: No unsafe-older() descriptor warning: an older(k) above 65535 blocks is imported silently
findings.core_does: MiniscriptDescriptor's constructor walks the node with ForEachNode and, for every OLDER fragment whose value part (k with SEQUENCE_LOCKTIME_TYPE_FLAG masked off) exceeds SEQUENCE_LOCKTIME_MASK (65535), records a warning: 'height-based relative locktime: older(N) > 65535 blocks is unsafe' or the 512-second equivalent (descriptor.cpp:1648-1661). ProcessDescriptorImport copies parsed_desc->Warnings() into the importdescriptors result (wallet/rpc/backup.cpp:243-245).
findings.we_do: %parse-miniscript-descriptor (descriptors.lisp:889-922) builds the node and runs %check-miniscript-sane; there is no ForEachNode walk and no descriptor-level warnings list. %process-descriptor-import has a warnings list (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:2181) but only ever pushes 'Range not given...', 'Not all private keys provided...' and 'Unknown output type...' into it.
findings.impact: BIP68 only carries 16 bits of relative-locktime value, so older(100000) is enforced as 100000 & 0xFFFF = 34464 blocks -- a lock roughly a third as long as written. Core tells the operator; we import it silently. Our script generation and our own ms-check-older both agree with consensus, so there is no split; the loss is that an operator sets up a recovery path they believe is ~2 years and get ~8 months with no indication.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval, warm image: parse-descriptor of wsh(and_v(v:pk(03d30199..),older(100000))) returned (:ACCEPTED T :VALID-P T :SANE-P T) with a 40-byte witnessScript and no warning channel; grep over src/wallet/wallet.lisp:2200-2280 shows the only three strings pushed into the import warnings list, none of them about older().

coverage_note: Oracle: 91 Test() vectors from refs/bitcoin/src/test/miniscript_tests.cpp:501-700, mechanically extracted and replayed in BOTH contexts (182 runs) through ms-parse / ms-node-script / the type predicates / ms-node-get-ops / ms-node-get-stack-size / ms-node-get-witness-size / ms-node-exec-stack-size / ms-from-script, plus the file's separate unit vectors (nonminpush, non-minimal VERIFY, the MINIMALIF thresh, the four duplicate-key cases, FindInsaneSub, the signed-number cases). 167 of the 182 runs matched Core exactly, including every expected script hex byte for byte. WHAT IS FAITHFUL, verified by execution: SanitizeType, the whole ComputeType calculus for all 26 fragments including the thresh timelock accumulator, ComputeScriptLen, script generation in both contexts (the x-only key rule for tapscript included), CalcOps, CalcStackSize (SatInfo netdiff/exec semiring), CalcWitnessSize, CheckOpsLimit, CheckStackSize in both its P2WSH and tapscript forms, IsValidTopLevel/IsNonMalleable/NeedsSignature/CheckTimeLocksMix/CheckDuplicateKey/IsSane/IsNotSatisfiable, FindInsaneSub's post-order choice, and the descriptor-level IsSane error branch order. ToString was checked by re-parsing all 107 valid vectors: 0 produced a different script and the 25 textual differences are all Core's own sugar normalizations (c:pk_k->pk, c:pk_h->pkh, or_i(0,X)->l:, and_v(X,1)->t:), verified line by line against miniscript.h:900-940. ProduceInput was diffed clause by clause against miniscript.h:1245-1440 and matches Core for every fragment except the missing MULTI_A (c9076fba). NOT COVERED: (a) the fuzz harness refs/bitcoin/src/test/fuzz/miniscript.cpp -- no differential fuzzing was run, so a random-expression comparison against Core's binary is still owed and belongs to the GA11 differential-harness lane; (b) Node::Satisfy's end-to-end correctness against the SCRIPT INTERPRETER -- I compared witness stacks against Core's algorithm but never executed a produced witness through our interpreter, which the script-interpreter dimension inherits; (c) how a miniscript descriptor registers key hashes and taproot spend data in the signing provider (Core MiniscriptDescriptor::MakeScripts, descriptor.cpp:1626-1641) -- that seam belongs to the descriptors+signing dimension, which should check that a tapscript pkh() leaf registers Hash160(XOnlyPubKey) and not the 33-byte key id; (d) multipath (BIP389) key-vector length matching inside a miniscript (descriptor.cpp:2640-2650), also the descriptors dimension; (e) the miniscript satisfier's `estimating` mode, which has no caller in src/ at all and so has no observable behaviour to compare; (f) Core's four SanitizeType CHECK_NONFATALs we do not assert (d conflicts with f, V implies f, K implies s, z implies m) -- they are internal consistency assertions about the calculus, and since all 91 vectors agree there is nothing to report; (g) node_deep_destruct-style stack safety (miniscript_tests.cpp:730) -- our tree walks are all plain recursion where Core's are explicit stacks, but the cubic cost of d722b087 makes a deep tree unreachable long before the control stack matters, so the two should be re-tested together after that fix.
